tools.name: get_test_address
tools.description:
Reserve a single-use address to send a draft email to, for a full check.

    Returns the address and the URL its report will appear at. The address
    accepts exactly one message and expires after an hour. The email has to be
    sent by the person, from the platform or mailbox they really send fr

tools.name: wait_for_report
tools.description:
Wait until the message arrives and has been analysed, then summarise it.

    Call it after the email has been sent to the address from
    get_test_address. Blocks rather than returning "not ready yet": an agent
    told to poll writes a sleep loop and usually gives up before the analysis
    finis

tools.name: get_report
tools.description:
Read a report by its slug without waiting, with provider placement so far.

    The report stays at its link for good and anyone with the link can read
    it: the checks, the score, the fix plan, and the subject and sender of
    the email.

tools.name: get_message_source
tools.description:
The message exactly as it was received: headers, both bodies, source.

    Useful when a finding points at a header and the agent needs to see what it
    actually sent rather than what it believes it sent. The message is kept
    for an hour after it arrives and then deleted; within that hour anyon

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_test_address, get_report, get_message_source · Public sink: get_test_address, wait_for_report, get_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_test_address, get_report, get_message_source · Public sink: get_test_address, wait_for_report, get_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_report" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet:
before: "Read a report by its slug without waiting, with provider placement so far.

    Works for one-hour tests and for letters in the person's series mailboxes." → after: "Read a report by its slug without waiting, with provider placement so far.

    The report stays at its link for good and anyone with the link can read
    it: the checks, the score, the fix plan, and the subject and sender of
    the email."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
